**Ethereum** is a [decentralized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralization#Blockchain_technology "Decentralization")[blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain") with [smart contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_contract "Smart contract") functionality. **Ether** ([abbreviation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217#Cryptocurrencies "ISO 4217"): **ETH**[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-3)) is the native [cryptocurrency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptocurrency "Cryptocurrency") of the platform. Among cryptocurrencies, ether is second only to [bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin "Bitcoin") in [market capitalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Market_capitalization "Market capitalization").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-ft20210528-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-wsj20210603-5) It is [open-source software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open-source_software "Open-source software").

Ethereum was conceived in 2013 by [programmer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_programming "Computer programming")[Vitalik Buterin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitalik_Buterin "Vitalik Buterin").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTETapscottTapscott201687-6) Other founders include [Gavin Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin_Wood "Gavin Wood"), [Charles Hoskinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Hoskinson "Charles Hoskinson"), [Anthony Di Iorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Di_Iorio "Anthony Di Iorio"), and [Joseph Lubin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Lubin_(entrepreneur) "Joseph Lubin (entrepreneur)").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-paumgarten-7) In 2014, [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development "Software development") work began and was [crowdfunded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdfunding "Crowdfunding"), and the network went live on 30 July 2015.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-8) Ethereum allows anyone to deploy [decentralized applications](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_application "Decentralized application") onto it, which anyone can then use.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-9)[Decentralized finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_finance "Decentralized finance") (DeFi) applications provide [financial instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_instrument "Financial instrument") that do not directly rely on [financial intermediaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_intermediary "Financial intermediary") like [brokerages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brokerage "Brokerage"), [exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exchange_(organized_market) "Exchange (organized market)"), or [banks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bank "Bank"). This facilitates borrowing against cryptocurrency holdings or lending them out for [interest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interest "Interest").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-10)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-fortune20210506-11) Ethereum allows users to create fungible (e.g. ERC-20) and [non-fungible tokens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token "Non-fungible token") (NFTs) with a variety of properties, and to create smart contracts that can receive, hold and send those assets in accordance with the contract's immutable code and a transaction's input data.

On 15 September 2022, Ethereum transitioned its [consensus mechanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consensus_(computer_science) "Consensus (computer science)") from [proof-of-work](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_of_work "Proof of work") (PoW) to [proof-of-stake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_of_stake "Proof of stake") (PoS) in an update known as "The Merge", which cut the blockchain's energy usage by over 99%.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-12)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-EnergyRevamp-13)

## History

### Founding (2013–2014)

[![Image 3](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1c/Vitalik_Buterin_TechCrunch_London_2015_%28cropped%29.jpg/330px-Vitalik_Buterin_TechCrunch_London_2015_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Vitalik_Buterin_TechCrunch_London_2015_(cropped).jpg)

Ethereum co-founder [Vitalik Buterin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitalik_Buterin "Vitalik Buterin") in 2015

Ethereum was initially described in late 2013 in a [white paper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_paper "White paper") by [Vitalik Buterin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitalik_Buterin "Vitalik Buterin"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTETapscottTapscott201687-6)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-14) a programmer and co-founder of _[Bitcoin Magazine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin\_Magazine "Bitcoin Magazine")_, that described a way to build [decentralized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized "Decentralized") applications.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Finley-27-Jan-2014-15)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Schneider-2014-04-07-16) Buterin argued to the [Bitcoin Core](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin_Core "Bitcoin Core") developers that blockchain technology could benefit from other applications besides money and that it needed a more robust language for application development[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-tapscott2016-17):88 that could lead to attaching[_[clarification needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Please\_clarify "Wikipedia:Please clarify")_][real-world assets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-World_Asset?action=edit&redlink=1 "Real-World Asset (page does not exist)"), such as stocks and property, to the blockchain.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Russo2020-18) In 2013, Buterin briefly worked with [eToro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EToro "EToro") CEO Yoni Assia on the [Colored Coins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colored_Coins "Colored Coins") project and drafted its white paper outlining additional use cases for blockchain technology.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTERusso202044-19) However, after failing to gain agreement on how the project should proceed, he proposed the development of a new platform with a more robust scripting language—a [Turing-complete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing-complete "Turing-complete") programming language[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTETapscottTapscott2016278-20)—that would eventually become Ethereum.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-tapscott2016-17)

Ethereum was announced at the North American Bitcoin Conference in Miami, in January 2014.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Paumgarten-21) During the conference, [Gavin Wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin_Wood "Gavin Wood"), [Charles Hoskinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Hoskinson "Charles Hoskinson"), and [Anthony Di Iorio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Di_Iorio "Anthony Di Iorio") (who financed the project) rented a house in Miami with Buterin at which they could develop a fuller sense of what Ethereum might become.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Paumgarten-21) Di Iorio invited friend [Joseph Lubin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_Lubin_(entrepreneur) "Joseph Lubin (entrepreneur)"), who invited reporter Morgen Peck, to bear witness.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Paumgarten-21) Peck subsequently wrote about the experience in _[Wired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wired\_(magazine) "Wired (magazine)")_.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-22) Six months later the founders met again in [Zug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zug "Zug"), Switzerland, where Buterin told the founders that the project would proceed as a non-profit. Hoskinson left the project at that time and soon after founded IOHK, a blockchain company responsible for [Cardano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardano_(blockchain_platform) "Cardano (blockchain platform)").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Paumgarten-21)

Ethereum has an unusually long list of founders.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-entrepreneur20210817-23) Anthony Di Iorio wrote: "Ethereum was founded by Vitalik Buterin, Myself, Charles Hoskinson, Mihai Alisie & Amir Chetrit (the initial 5) in December 2013. Joseph Lubin, Gavin Wood, & Jeffrey Wilcke were added in early 2014 as founders." Buterin chose the name Ethereum after browsing [a list of elements from science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_fictional_elements,_materials,_isotopes_and_subatomic_particles "List of fictional elements, materials, isotopes and subatomic particles") on [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia "Wikipedia"). He stated, "I immediately realized that I liked it better than all of the other alternatives that I had seen; I suppose it was that [it] sounded nice and it had the word '[ether](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luminiferous_aether "Luminiferous aether")', referring to the hypothetical invisible medium that permeates the universe and allows light to travel."[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Paumgarten-21) Buterin wanted his platform to be the underlying and imperceptible medium for the applications running on top of it.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTERusso202056-24)

### Development (2014)

Formal development of the software underlying Ethereum began in early 2014 through a Swiss company, Ethereum Switzerland GmbH (_EthSuisse_).[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloomberg20160820-25)The idea of putting executable [smart contracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_contract "Smart contract") in the blockchain needed to be specified before it could be implemented in software. This work was done by Gavin Wood, then the [chief technology officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_technology_officer "Chief technology officer"), in the Ethereum Yellow Paper that specified the Ethereum Virtual Machine.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Dannen2018-26)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-eip150-27) Subsequently, a Swiss non-profit foundation, the **Ethereum Foundation** (_Stiftung Ethereum_), was founded. Development was funded by an online public crowd sale from July to August 2014, in which participants bought the Ethereum value token (ether) with another digital currency, [bitcoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bitcoin "Bitcoin"). While there was early praise for the technical innovations of Ethereum, questions were also raised about its security and scalability.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Finley-27-Jan-2014-15)

The Foundation funded multiple teams in different cities building three separate implementations of the protocol: Geth ([Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language) "Go (programming language)")), Pyethereum ([Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) "Python (programming language)")), a [C++](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++ "C++") implementation, and also Swarm ([decentralized file storage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_file_storage "Decentralized file storage")), Mist Browser (A wallet, [browser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_browser "File browser") and a user interface for smart contracts, now defunct) among other projects. The intended purpose of the three distinct implementations would be so that if one of them had a bug, the other two could be used as a comparison.

### Launch and the DAO event (2014–2016)

Several codenamed prototypes of Ethereum were developed over 18 months in 2014 and 2015 by the Ethereum Foundation as part of their [proof-of-concept](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_of_concept#Software_development "Proof of concept") series.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTETapscottTapscott201687-6) "Olympic" was the last prototype and public beta pre-release. The Olympic network gave users a [bug bounty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bug_bounty "Bug bounty") of 25,000 ether for stress-testing the Ethereum blockchain. On 30 July 2015, "Frontier" marked the official launch of the Ethereum platform, and Ethereum created its "genesis block".[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-FOOTNOTETapscottTapscott201687-6)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-WSJFRONTIER-28) The genesis block contained 8,893 transactions allocating various amounts of ether to different addresses, and a block reward of 5 ETH.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since the initial launch, Ethereum has undergone a number of planned protocol upgrades, which are important changes affecting the underlying functionality and/or [incentive structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incentive_compatibility "Incentive compatibility") of the platform.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-EFPROCESS-29)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-30) Protocol upgrades are accomplished by means of a [hard fork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_fork "Hard fork").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In 2016, a [decentralized autonomous organization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_autonomous_organization "Decentralized autonomous organization") called [The DAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_DAO_(organization) "The DAO (organization)")—a set of smart contracts developed on the platform—raised a record US$150 million in a [crowd sale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Token_sale "Token sale") to fund the project.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-WSJDAOCC-31)[Emin Gün Sirer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emin_G%C3%BCn_Sirer "Emin Gün Sirer"), Vlad Zamfir and Dino Mark had written a paper called _A Call for a Temporary Moratorium on The DAO_ in which they described in which way the DAO might be vunerable to attacks.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-DAO_paper-32) The DAO was exploited in June 2016 when US$50 million of DAO tokens were stolen by an unknown hacker.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-NYTDAOHACK-33)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-BIDAOHACK-34) The event sparked a debate in the crypto-community about whether Ethereum should perform a contentious "hard fork" to reappropriate the affected funds.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-IEEEDAOHK-35) The fork resulted in the network splitting into two blockchains: Ethereum with the theft reversed, and [Ethereum Classic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum_Classic "Ethereum Classic") which continued on the original chain.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloomberg20170613-36)

### Continued development and milestones (2017–present)

In March 2017, various [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain") startups, research groups, and [_Fortune_ 500](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune_500 "Fortune 500") companies announced the creation of the Enterprise Ethereum Alliance (EEA) with 30 founding members.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-NYTEEA-37) By May 2017, the nonprofit organization had 116 enterprise members, including [ConsenSys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ConsenSys "ConsenSys"), [CME Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CME_Group "CME Group"), [Cornell University's research group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornell_University#Research "Cornell University"), [Toyota Research Institute](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toyota_Group "Toyota Group"), [Samsung SDS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samsung_SDS "Samsung SDS"), [Microsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft "Microsoft"), [Intel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intel "Intel"), [J. P. Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JPMorgan_Chase "JPMorgan Chase"), [Cooley LLP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cooley_LLP "Cooley LLP"), [Merck KGaA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merck_KGaA "Merck KGaA"), [DTCC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depository_Trust_&_Clearing_Corporation "Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation"), [Deloitte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deloitte "Deloitte"), [Accenture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accenture "Accenture"), [Banco Santander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banco_Santander "Banco Santander"), [BNY Mellon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BNY_Mellon "BNY Mellon"), [ING](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ING_Group "ING Group"), and [National Bank of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Bank_of_Canada "National Bank of Canada").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-IEEEEEA-38)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-EEA022217-39) By July 2017, there were over 150 members in the alliance, including [MasterCard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MasterCard "MasterCard"), [Cisco Systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cisco_Systems "Cisco Systems"), [Sberbank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sberbank "Sberbank"), and [Scotiabank](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scotiabank "Scotiabank").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-40)

In 2024, Paul Brody, EEA board member for EY, was announced as the new chairperson, and Karen Scarbrough, board member for Microsoft, as the new executive director. Vanessa Grellet from Arche Capital also joined as a new board member.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-41)

#### _CryptoKitties_ and the ERC-721 NFT standard

In 2017, _[CryptoKitties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoKitties "CryptoKitties")_, the [blockchain game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain_game "Blockchain game") and [decentralized application](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_application "Decentralized application") (dApp) featuring digital cat artwork as [NFTs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token "Non-fungible token"), was launched on the Ethereum network.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-42) In cultivating popularity with users and collectors, it gained notable mainstream media attention providing significant exposure to Ethereum in the process.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-43) It was considered the most popular smart contract in use on the network[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-44) but it also highlighted concerns over Ethereum's scalability due to the game's substantial consumption of network capacity at the time.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-45)

In January 2018, a community-driven paper (an EIP, "Ethereum Improvement Proposal") under the leadership of [civic hacker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacker#Civic_hacker "Hacker") and lead author [William Entriken](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Entriken "William Entriken") was published, called _ERC-721: Non-Fungible Token Standard._[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-46) It introduced [ERC-721](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ERC-721 "ERC-721"), the first official NFT standard on Ethereum.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-47) This standardization allowed Ethereum to become central to a multi-billion dollar digital collectibles market.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-48)

#### Continued developments

By January 2018, ether was the second-largest cryptocurrency in terms of market capitalization, behind bitcoin.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-fortune20180108-49)As of 2021, it maintained that relative position.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-ft20210528-4)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-wsj20210603-5)

In 2019, Ethereum Foundation employee [Virgil Griffith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virgil_Griffith "Virgil Griffith") was arrested by the US government for presenting at a blockchain conference in North Korea.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-50) He would later plead guilty to one count of conspiring to violate the International Emergency Economic Powers Act in 2021.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-51)

In March 2021, [Visa Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc.") announced that it began settling [stablecoin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stablecoin "Stablecoin") transactions using Ethereum.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-fortune20210329-52) In April 2021, [JP Morgan Chase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JP_Morgan_Chase "JP Morgan Chase"), [UBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UBS "UBS"), and [MasterCard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MasterCard "MasterCard") announced that they were investing US$65 million into [ConsenSys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ConsenSys "ConsenSys"), a software development firm that builds Ethereum-related infrastructure.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-fortune20210413-53)

There were two network upgrades in 2021. The first was "Berlin", implemented on 14 April 2021.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bi20210413-54) The second was "London", which took effect on 5 August.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-cnbc20210805-55) The London upgrade included Ethereum Improvement Proposal ("EIP") 1559, a mechanism for reducing transaction fee [volatility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volatility_(finance) "Volatility (finance)"). The mechanism causes a portion of the ether paid in transaction fees for each block to be destroyed rather than given to the block proposer, reducing the inflation rate of ether and potentially resulting in periods of deflation.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloomberg20210307-56)

On 27 August 2021, the blockchain experienced a brief [fork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fork_(blockchain) "Fork (blockchain)") that was the result of clients running different incompatible software versions.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloom20210827-57)

### Transition to proof-of-stake

[![Image 4](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e9/Ethereum_Merge_Party_in_San_Francisco_in_2022.jpg/250px-Ethereum_Merge_Party_in_San_Francisco_in_2022.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ethereum_Merge_Party_in_San_Francisco_in_2022.jpg)

Ethereum enthusiasts gather for a Merge party in San Francisco in 2022.

"The Merge" (formerly called Ethereum 2.0) was a set of three updates (Bellatrix, Paris, and Shapella) that transitioned Ethereum's consensus protocol from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake. Bellatrix updated the proof-of-stake Beacon chain and introduced economic slashing. Paris was the event at block 15537393 on 15 September 2022 that merged Ethereum to the Beacon chain. Shapella (Shanghai-Capella) was the update that allowed for staking withdrawals.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-58)

The switch from proof-of-work to proof-of-stake has cut Ethereum's energy usage by over 99%.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-59) However, the effect this has on [global energy consumption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Global_energy_consumption "Global energy consumption") and climate change may be limited since the computers previously used for mining ether may be used to mine other cryptocurrencies that are energy-intensive.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-EnergyRevamp-13)

### Post-Merge updates

#### Dencun

On 13 March 2024, "Dencun" or also "Deneb-Cancun" set of upgrades went live. These included EIP-4844[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-eip4844-60) (Proto-Danksharding) which introduced "blobs" that can be used for general-purpose data-availability. ## Design

### Overview

Ethereum is a [peer-to-peer network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-to-peer_network "Peer-to-peer network") that maintains a [database](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Database "Database") containing the storage values of all Ethereum accounts and processes state-altering transactions.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-64) Approximately every 12 seconds, a batch of new transactions, known as a "block", is processed by the network. Each block contains a [cryptographic hash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_hash_function "Cryptographic hash function") identifying the series of blocks that must precede it if the block is to be considered valid. This series of blocks is known as the [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain").[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-65)

Each "node" (network participant) connects with a relatively small subset of the network to offer blocks and unvalidated transactions (i.e. transactions not yet in the blockchain) to its peers for download, and it downloads any from its peers that it doesn't already have. Each node usually has a unique set of peers, so that offering an item to its peers results in the propagation of that item throughout the entire network within seconds. A node's collection of unvalidated transactions is known as its "mempool".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-66)

A node may choose to create a copy of the state for itself. It does this by starting with the genesis state and executing every transaction in the blockchain, in the proper order of blocks and in the order they are listed within each block.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-67)

Any Ethereum account may "stake" (deposit) 32 or more ETH to register a "validator". At the end of each "epoch" (32 block slots, each slot lasting 12 seconds), each validator is [pseudorandomly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pseudorandomness "Pseudorandomness") assigned to one of the slots of the epoch after the next, either as the block proposer or as an attester. During a slot, the block proposer uses their mempool to create a block that is intended to become the new "head" (latest block) of the blockchain, and the attesters attest to which block is at the head of the chain. If a validator makes self-contradicting proposals or attestations, or if it is inactive, it loses a portion of its stake. Any Ethereum account may send ETH to a validator at any time to increase its stake. A validator's attestation is given a weight equal to its stake or 2,048, whichever is less. According to the Ethereum protocol, the blockchain with the highest accumulated weight of attestations at any given time is to be regarded as the canonical chain. Validators are rewarded for making valid proposals and attestations. A validator's rewards are paid via transactions within the same chain that contains their proposal or attestation, and therefore would have little or no market value unless that chain becomes the canonical chain. This incentivizes validators to support the chain that they think other validators view as the canonical chain, which results in a high degree of consensus.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-68)

### Ether

Ether (ETH) is the cryptocurrency generated in accordance with the Ethereum protocol as a reward to validators in a [proof-of-stake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proof_of_stake "Proof of stake") system for adding blocks to the blockchain. Ether is represented in the state as an [unsigned](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signedness "Signedness")[integer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integer_(computer_science) "Integer (computer science)") associated with each account, this being the account's ETH balance denominated in wei (10 18 wei = 1 ether). At the end of each epoch, new ETH is generated by the addition of protocol-specified amounts to the balances of all validators that made valid block proposals or attestations in the epoch before the last (i.e. the epoch being finalized). Additionally, ether is the only currency accepted by the protocol as payment for the transaction fee. The transaction fee is composed of two parts: the base fee and the tip. The base fee is "burned" (deleted from existence) and the tip goes to the block proposer. The validator reward together with the tips provide the incentive to validators to keep the blockchain growing (i.e. to keep processing new transactions). Therefore, ETH is fundamental to the operation of the network. Ether may be "sent" from one account to another via a transaction, the execution of which simply entails subtracting the _amount to be sent_ from the sender's balance and adding the same amount to the recipient's balance.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-NYTEVCRB-69)

Ether is often erroneously referred to as "Ethereum".[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-70)

The uppercase Greek letter [Xi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xi_(letter) "Xi (letter)"), Ξ, is sometimes used as a [currency symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Currency_symbol "Currency symbol") for ether.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Accounts

There are two types of accounts on Ethereum: user accounts (also known as externally-owned accounts), and contract accounts. Both types have an ETH balance, may transfer ETH to any account, may execute the code of another contract, or create a new contract, and are identified on the blockchain and in the state by an account address.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloomberg20201125-71)

Contracts are the only type of account that has associated [bytecode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bytecode "Bytecode") and storage (to store contract-specific state). The code of a contract is evaluated when a transaction is sent to it. The code of the contract may read user-specified data from the transaction, and may have a [return value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return_statement "Return statement"). In addition to [control flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Control_flow "Control flow") statements, the bytecode may include instructions to send ETH, read from and write to the contract's storage, create temporary storage ([memory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volatile_memory "Volatile memory")) that vanishes at the end of code evaluation, perform [arithmetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arithmetic "Arithmetic") and hashing operations, send transaction-like calls to other contracts (thus executing their code), create new contracts, and query information about the current transaction or the blockchain.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-72)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_]

#### Addresses

Ethereum account addresses are composed of the prefix "`0x`" (a common identifier for [hexadecimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hexadecimal "Hexadecimal")) concatenated with the rightmost 20 bytes of the [Keccak-256](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SHA-3 "SHA-3") hash of the [ECDSA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elliptic_Curve_Digital_Signature_Algorithm "Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm")[public key](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public-key_cryptography "Public-key cryptography") (the curve used is the so-called _secp256k1_). In hexadecimal, two digits represent a byte, and so addresses contain 40 hexadecimal digits after the "`0x`", e.g. `0xb794f5ea0ba39494ce839613fffba74279579268`. Contract addresses are in the same format, however, they are determined by sender and creation transaction [nonce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cryptographic_nonce "Cryptographic nonce").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-73)

### Virtual machine

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Ethereum_Transactions_Chart.png/500px-Ethereum_Transactions_Chart.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ethereum_Transactions_Chart.png)

The number of daily confirmed Ethereum transactions as of February 2024

The Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) is the [runtime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Runtime_(program_lifecycle_phase) "Runtime (program lifecycle phase)") environment for transaction execution in Ethereum. The EVM is a [stack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_(abstract_data_type) "Stack (abstract data type)") based virtual machine with an [instruction set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instruction_set_architecture "Instruction set architecture") specifically designed for Ethereum. The instruction set includes, among other things, stack operations, memory operations, and operations to inspect the current execution context, such as remaining gas, information about the current block, and the current transaction. The EVM is designed to be [deterministic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deterministic_algorithm "Deterministic algorithm") on a wide variety of [hardware](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_hardware "Computer hardware") and [operating systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Operating_system "Operating system"), so that given a pre-transaction state and a transaction, each node produces the same post-transaction state, thereby enabling network consensus. The formal definition of the EVM is specified in the Ethereum Yellow Paper.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-eip150-27)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-DEBA20-74) EVMs have been implemented in [C++](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C++ "C++"), [C#](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_Sharp_(programming_language) "C Sharp (programming language)"), [Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Go_(programming_language) "Go (programming language)"), [Haskell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haskell_(programming_language) "Haskell (programming language)"), [Java](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Java_(programming_language) "Java (programming language)"), [JavaScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript "JavaScript"), [Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Python_(programming_language) "Python (programming language)"), [Ruby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruby_(programming_language) "Ruby (programming language)"), [Rust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(programming_language) "Rust (programming language)"), [Elixir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elixir_(programming_language) "Elixir (programming language)"), [Erlang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erlang_(programming_language) "Erlang (programming language)"), and soon[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_][WebAssembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebAssembly "WebAssembly").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Gas

Gas is a [unit of account](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unit_of_account "Unit of account") within the EVM used in the calculation of the transaction fee, which is the amount of ETH a transaction's sender must pay to the network to have the transaction included in the blockchain. Each type of operation which may be performed by the EVM is [hardcoded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hardcoded "Hardcoded") with a certain gas cost, which is intended to be roughly [proportional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proportionality_(mathematics) "Proportionality (mathematics)") to the monetary value of the resources (e.g. [computation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computation "Computation") and [storage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_data_storage "Computer data storage")) a node must expend or dedicate to perform that operation.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-75)[_[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No\_original\_research#Primary,\_secondary\_and\_tertiary\_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")_]

When a sender is creating a transaction, the sender must specify a _gas limit_ and _gas price_. The _gas limit_ is the maximum amount of gas the sender is willing to use in the transaction, and the _gas price_ is the amount of ETH the sender wishes to pay to the network per unit of gas used. A transaction may only be included in the blockchain at a block slot that has a _base gas price_ less than or equal to the transaction's _gas price_. The portion of the _gas price_ that is in excess of the _base gas price_ is known as the tip and goes to the block proposer; the higher the tip, the more incentive a block proposer has to include the transaction in their block, and thus the quicker the transaction will be included in the blockchain. The sender buys the full amount of gas (i.e. their ETH balance is debited _gas limit_ × _gas price_ and their gas balance is set to _gas limit_) up-front, at the start of the execution of the transaction, and is refunded at the end for any unused gas. If at any point the transaction does not have enough gas to perform the next operation, the transaction is reverted but the sender is still only refunded for the unused gas. In [user interfaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/User_interface "User interface"), gas prices are typically denominated in gigawei (Gwei), a subunit of ETH equal to 10−9 ETH.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-76)

## Applications

The EVM's [instruction set](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instruction_set "Instruction set") is [Turing-complete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turing_completeness "Turing completeness").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-eip150-27) Popular uses of Ethereum have included the creation of fungible (ERC-20) and non-fungible (ERC-721) tokens with a variety of properties, [crowdfunding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crowdfunding "Crowdfunding") (e.g. [initial coin offerings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_coin_offerings "Initial coin offerings")), [decentralized finance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_finance "Decentralized finance"), [decentralized exchanges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_exchange "Decentralized exchange"), [decentralized autonomous organizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_autonomous_organization "Decentralized autonomous organization") (DAOs), games, [prediction markets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prediction_market "Prediction market"), and gambling.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

### Contract source code

Ethereum's smart contracts are written in [high-level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-level_programming_language "High-level programming language") programming languages and then [compiled](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compiler "Compiler") down to EVM [bytecode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bytecode "Bytecode"), which is then deployed to the Ethereum blockchain. They can be written in [Solidity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solidity "Solidity") (a language library with similarities to [C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C_(programming_language) "C (programming language)") and [JavaScript](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JavaScript "JavaScript")), as well as others. Source code and compiler information are usually published on blockchain explorer websites soon after the launch of the contract so that users can see the code and verify that it compiles to the bytecode that is on-chain.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-77)[_[non-primary source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:No\_original\_research#Primary,\_secondary\_and\_tertiary\_sources "Wikipedia:No original research")_]

One issue related to using smart contracts on a public blockchain is that bugs, including security holes, are visible to all but cannot be fixed quickly.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Peck20160528-78) One example of this is the 2016 attack on [The DAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_DAO_(organization) "The DAO (organization)"), which could not be quickly stopped or reversed.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-NYTDAOHACK-33)

### ERC-20 tokens

The ERC-20 (Ethereum Request-for-Comments #20) Token Standard allows for [fungible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungible "Fungible") tokens on the Ethereum [blockchain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockchain "Blockchain"). The standard, proposed by Fabian Vogelsteller in November 2015, implements an [API](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/API "API") for tokens within [smart contracts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_contract "Smart contract"). The standard provides functions that include the transfer of tokens from one account to another, getting the current token balance of an account, and getting the total supply of the token available on the network. Smart contracts that correctly implement ERC-20 processes are called ERC-20 Token Contracts, and they keep track of created tokens on Ethereum. Numerous cryptocurrencies have launched as ERC-20 tokens and have been distributed through [initial coin offerings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Initial_coin_offerings "Initial coin offerings").[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-forbes20200728-79)

### Non-fungible tokens (NFTs)

Ethereum also allows for the creation of unique and indivisible tokens, called [non-fungible tokens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-fungible_token "Non-fungible token") (NFTs).[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-80) Since tokens of this type are unique, they have been used to represent such things as collectibles, digital art, sports memorabilia, virtual real estate, and items within games.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-81) ERC-721 is the first official NFT standard for Ethereum and was followed up by ERC-1155 which introduced semi-fungibility; both are widely used,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-82) though some fully fungible tokens using ERC-20 have been used for NFTs such as _[CryptoPunks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoPunks "CryptoPunks")_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-83)

The first NFT project, Etheria, a 3D map of tradable and customizable hexagonal tiles, was deployed to the network in October 2015 and demonstrated live at DEVCON1 in November of that year.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-84) In 2021, [Christie's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christie's "Christie's") sold a digital image with an NFT by [Beeple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beeple "Beeple") for US$69.3 million, making him the [third-most-valuable living artist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_most_expensive_artworks_by_living_artists "List of most expensive artworks by living artists") in terms of [auction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_auction "Art auction") prices at the time, although observers have noted that both the buyer and seller had a vested interest in driving demand for the artist's work.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-85)[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-86)

### Decentralized finance

Decentralized finance (DeFi) offers [financial instruments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Financial_instrument "Financial instrument") in a decentralized architecture, outside of companies' and governments' control, such as money market funds which let users earn interest.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-forbes20190426-87) DeFi applications are typically accessed through a [Web3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web3 "Web3")-enabled browser extension or application, such as [MetaMask](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MetaMask "MetaMask"), which allows users to directly interact with the Ethereum blockchain through a website.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloomberg20200902-88) Many of these DApps can connect and work together to create complex financial services.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-bloomberg20200826-89)

Examples of DeFi platforms include [MakerDAO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MakerDAO?action=edit&redlink=1 "MakerDAO (page does not exist)").[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-fortune20200825-90)[Uniswap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uniswap "Uniswap"), a [decentralized exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decentralized_exchange "Decentralized exchange") for tokens on Ethereum grew from US$20 million in liquidity to US$2.9 billion in 2020.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-forbes20201018-91) As of October 2020, over US$11 billion was invested in various DeFi protocols.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Zcash-92) Additionally, through a process called "wrapping", certain DeFi protocols allow synthetic versions of various assets (such as bitcoin, gold, and oil) to be tradeable on Ethereum and also compatible with all of Ethereum's major wallets and applications.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-Zcash-92)

[Aave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aave "Aave") is a protocol for [microlending](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microlending "Microlending") using Ethereum.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-93)

### Performance and scalability

As of December 2025, the maximum theoretical throughput for Ethereum L1 is 238 TPS (given its current 60M gas limit, 12s blocks, and 21k gas cost for ETH transfers). Due to large smart contract and batch transaction using more gas in each block, the average transaction throughput is much less. As of January 2016, the Ethereum averaged about 25 transactions per second; this did not change after the move to proof-of-stake. In comparison, the [Visa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visa_Inc. "Visa Inc.") payment platform processes 45,000 payments per second. This has led some to question the scalability of Ethereum.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-100)

Ethereum's blockchain uses a [Merkle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merkle_tree "Merkle tree")–Patricia Tree to store account state in each block.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-101) The trie allows for storage savings, set membership proofs (called "Merkle proofs"), and light client synchronization. The network has faced congestion problems, such as in 2017 in relation to _[CryptoKitties](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CryptoKitties "CryptoKitties")_.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-102)

Layer 2 (L2) is one of the approaches that the Ethereum ecosystem has developed in order to scale up and handle more transactions with lower transaction fees.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-103) A Layer 2 chain is a separate blockchain that extends Ethereum (Layer 1) and inherits the security guarantees of Ethereum.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-104) There are different types of L2 chains, including optimistic rollups and zero-knowledge rollups (zk rollups).[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-105)[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-106)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-107) Depending on their individual technical details, some L2 chains are capable of processing thousands of transactions per second.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-108)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-109)

## Legal status and regulation

The legal status of ether (ETH), Ethereum's native token, remains subject to uncertainty and varies substantially from one jurisdiction to another.

In the United States, regulatory authorities have increasingly signaled that ether should be treated as a commodity under the jurisdiction of the [Commodity Futures Trading Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commodity_Futures_Trading_Commission "Commodity Futures Trading Commission") (CFTC). The CFTC has repeatedly asserted its regulatory authority over Ethereum, with former CFTC Chairman Heath Tarbert stating in 2019 that "ETH is a commodity" and subsequent leadership maintaining this position.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-110)[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-111)

From a private law perspective, many jurisdictions have recognized ether as a form of intangible personal property that can be owned, transferred, and used as collateral, similar to other forms of personal property.[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-112) In the United States specifically, the 2022 Amendments to the Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) introduced "controllable electronic records" (CERs) as a new category of personal property that includes digital assets like ether. Under UCC Article 12, ETH is classified as a CER, which provides a comprehensive framework for its commercial circulation.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethereum#cite_note-113)
